newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE DEFENDS UNDER-FIRE ROWELL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE DEFENDS UNDER-FIRE ROWELL.

text.p: England captain Phil de Glanville hit back at critics of coach Jack Rowell on Thursday as his team began the countdown to their opening Five Nations encounter with Scotland at Twickenham this weekend.

De Glanville and his squad have been irritated by claims that Rowell and the players are on a different wavelength and dismissed accusations from former team manager Geoff Cooke that Rowell talks tactical "munbo-jumbo."
"I don't know why people are trying to push for cracks that don't exist," said de Glanville, preparing for his first Five Nations game in charge.

"I don't know why people say these things, particularly three days before an international, and particularly people who have been involved in the England set-up and know how potentially disruptive that can be."

Another former national coach Dick Best launched a similar printed attack on Rowell just before the Italy game in November and de Glanville advised any future mud-slingers to hold their fire until a non-international week.

"It's needless. If people have their own views they can say what they like, but their timing could have been better. I don't know what people are on but maybe they want to look at their calendars a bit more carefully.
"We're very clear how we want to play the game and how Jack wants us to play it."

Rowell has done his best to ignore the criticism this week, simply pointing to his coaching record which yielded 16 domestic trophies at Bath and Five Nations championship success in both his two seasons in charge.
His chances of making that a hat-trick depend on England improving dramatically on their display against Argentina before Christmas, starting with a record eighth straight win over the Scots.
The Twickenham crowd booed England off the pitch after the Pumas encounter but de Glanville, who missed the match through injury, insists the immediate future is "not all doom and gloom."
"A lot of good things came out of the games we played before Christmas and I hope we can carry those good things into the Five Nations."
